data.narrative:
Kyoto Fusioneering is a Series C nuclear energy company founded by Satoshi Konishi that has raised $125M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 11 comparable companies across nuclear energy—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and Fuse Energy.

Of the two valuation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. The peer-median approach was not used because the narrow peer set filtered by stage, proximity, and valuation tier yielded insufficient datapoints (fewer than 3 required for statistical reliability). Stage-progression applies a 1.7x multiplier to the $125M total capital raised as a proxy baseline, yielding an implied valuation of $212M.

The triangulation analysis supports a range of $181M (low) to $244M (high), with a median of $212M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single method rather than convergence across multiple approaches. The primary uncertainty is the absence of same-stage comparable transaction data in the nuclear energy sector, which constrains validation of the 1.7x step-up assumption. Material risks to valuation include technology risk on fusion timing, regulatory pathway clarity, and capital intensity at subsequent funding rounds.
